title: Mouth Emoji 👄 Meaning: Kisses, Lips and the Stare Meme
description: 👄 is a pair of red lips used for kisses, beauty and lipstick talk, flirting, and as the mouth in the 👁️👄👁️ meme. See what it means and how it differs from 💋.
summary: 👄 shows closed red lips. People use it for kissing and flirting, for beauty topics such as lipstick, lip gloss and fillers, and for anything about talking or keeping quiet. It is also the middle of the 👁️👄👁️ face, a blank stare used when something awkward or shocking happens.
meaning: The mouth emoji is glamorous by design: full, lipsticked and slightly pouty. That makes it a natural fit for beauty content. Makeup artists, lip product brands and anyone posting a new shade use 👄 literally, and it is common in conversations about lip fillers, lip liner tricks and skincare. In that setting it is simply a picture of the feature being discussed.

In messages between people who like each other, 👄 means a kiss or a suggestion of one. It is a little more sultry than 😘 because it isolates the lips rather than showing a cheerful face. Combined with other body-part or suggestive emojis it can become openly sexual, but a single 👄 at the end of a goodnight text is closer to “kisses” than to anything explicit.

It also represents speech. “Watch your 👄,” “he’s all 👄” and “my 👄 is shut” use the emoji as the word mouth, covering gossip, talking too much and keeping secrets. Food posts occasionally borrow it for “mouth-watering,” though 😋 and 🤤 are more usual there. In all of these the lips are a stand-in for the noun, a small rebus, and the glamorous styling is beside the point.

Since 2020, a large share of its appearances come from 👁️👄👁️, where it supplies the expressionless mouth of a face watching something unfold in silence. In that meme the lips have no romantic meaning at all. Spin-offs replace or surround the mouth for different moods, but the original trio remains the most recognizable use of 👄 online. Anyone who learned the emoji through that meme may be surprised to receive it as a kiss.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Partners and flirty friends send 👄 as a kiss, often after “mwah” or at the end of a message. Used in a sentence, it tends to mean talk: “you and your big 👄.” A row of them can be teasing or seductive depending on the relationship, so consider how the person usually messages you before assuming either.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Beauty creators caption lip tutorials, lipstick swatches and before-and-after filler videos with 👄. It appears in usernames and bios for makeup artists and aesthetic clinics. Everywhere else on these apps, the emoji is most likely part of 👁️👄👁️ in a caption or comment reacting to something awkward. Clinics and cosmetic injectors rely on it heavily as a quick visual label for their specialty.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: 👄 from someone you are interested in is clearly flirtatious. It focuses on lips and kissing rather than general affection, so it is bolder than a heart. If it arrives with compliments about how you look, the intent is hard to mistake. If it arrives as 👁️👄👁️, they are just reacting to something weird.

examples.meaning: Sending a kiss to a partner before bed.
Literal beauty use, showing off a lip product.

examples.text: Me when the teacher calls on me and I wasn’t listening 👁️👄👁️
examples.meaning: Frozen, blank-faced panic in an awkward moment.
Calling out a person who gossips or reveals secrets.

examples.text: Can’t stop thinking about last night 👄
examples.meaning: Flirtatious reference to kissing or intimacy.

combos.meaning: A vacant stare at something awkward, absurd or uncomfortable.
Lipstick and makeup, getting ready or showing a beauty look.
Lips are sealed; promising to keep a secret.
Lots of kisses, usually between partners.

confusedWith.difference: 💋 is the lipstick print left behind by a kiss, used to sign off affectionately. 👄 is the mouth itself, so it also covers speech, beauty and the stare meme, not only kissing.
🫦 shows teeth biting the lower lip and signals desire, flirtation or nervous tension. 👄 is a neutral closed mouth that needs context to become suggestive.

👅 sticks out and suggests licking, tasting or cheeky teasing. 👄 keeps the lips closed and leans toward kissing, talking and cosmetics. Used together they become much more explicit than either is alone.

avoid: Do not send it to coworkers or acquaintances, where lips on their own read as a come-on.
Avoid it with people who have not shown romantic interest, since it is more forward than a smiley or a heart.
In serious conversations about speaking up or staying silent, use words instead of a glossy pair of lips.
design: Every major platform draws a closed mouth with full lips, generally in red or deep pink as if wearing lipstick, and no surrounding face. The shape and shade differ slightly, with some versions glossier or more coral than others. Because it shows only lips, the emoji does not take skin tone modifiers.

faqs.q: What does 👄 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Most often a kiss or flirtation. He is signalling attraction and probably hoping you respond in kind. If the conversation is about someone talking too much, he means mouth literally, and if it appears between two eyes, he is using the stare meme.

faqs.q: What does 👄 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: It depends on the topic. With a selfie or a product mention it is about lips and makeup. Sent to someone she likes, it is a flirty kiss. Among friends it can be a playful “mwah” with no romantic intent.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 👄 and 💋?
faqs.a: 💋 is a kiss mark, the imprint lips leave, and it works like a signature kiss. 👄 depicts actual lips. Use 💋 to sign off with a kiss and 👄 when you mean the mouth, lips as a feature, or a more sultry tone.

It can be, particularly next to 👅, 🍆 or 💦, where it refers to oral sex. Alone it is usually milder: a kiss, lipstick, or talking. The emoji is suggestive enough that it is best kept to people you are close to.
